title: Subdomain Visit Count
spaceBreakdown:
- unordered_map<string,int> counts: up to ~3N entries, each key up to L chars → O(N × L)
- temporary string `domain`: O(L) per iteration, reused
- result vector: not counted (returned output)
- recursion depth: none
approach: Each count-paired domain contributes its visit count to every subdomain - the full domain and every suffix that starts after a dot. We use a hash map to accumulate counts per subdomain string, iterating over each character of the domain to find dots and extract suffixes via `substr`. Finally, we format each map entry as `"count domain"` and return. This is correct because every subdomain of a domain is exactly the full string or a suffix beginning right after some dot.
hints: Looking at "discuss.leetcode.com" and its implicit visits to "leetcode.com" and "com", what relationship does each visited domain have to the original full domain string?

Use an `unordered_map<string,int>` to accumulate visit counts per subdomain. For "9001 discuss.leetcode.com", add 9001 to "discuss.leetcode.com", then to "leetcode.com" (suffix after the first dot), then to "com" (suffix after the second dot).

```
counts = empty map
for each "rep domain" in cpdomains:
    counts[domain] += rep
    for each index i where domain[i] == '.':
        counts[domain[i+1 :]] += rep
return ["{count} {domain}" for each (domain, count) in counts]
```

**Two-level domain (minimum)** - only one dot, so just two subdomains
`Input: ["1 a.com"]` → `Expected: ["1 a.com","1 com"]`
⚠️ Bug: adding only suffixes after dots but skipping the full domain itself → returns `["1 com"]`

**Three-level domain** - two dots, three subdomains to extract
`Input: ["100 a.b.c"]` → `Expected: ["100 a.b.c","100 b.c","100 c"]`
⚠️ Bug: calling `find('.')` once instead of scanning every character → returns `["100 a.b.c","100 b.c"]`

**Duplicate domains** - same domain string appears in multiple entries
`Input: ["5 leet.com","5 leet.com"]` → `Expected: ["10 leet.com","10 com"]`
⚠️ Bug: using `map[domain] = rep` instead of `map[domain] += rep` → returns `["5 leet.com","5 com"]`

followUps.q: If the output must be sorted by visit count descending (ties broken alphabetically), how does the complexity change?
followUps.a: After building the hash map, extract all entries into a vector and sort with a custom comparator. This adds O(K log K) time where K is the number of unique subdomains (at most 3N), so total TC becomes O(N×L + K log K). Space stays O(N×L).

followUps.q: If cpdomains arrives as an unbounded stream and memory is limited, how would you adapt?
followUps.a: Process entries in fixed-size batches, each time building a local hash map and flushing accumulated counts to disk keyed by subdomain. After the stream ends, merge the disk-based partial counts. TC per batch is O(batch × L); total disk I/O is O(N × L).

followUps.q: If you must also answer queries like "total visits to all subdomains of com", how would you extend the structure?
followUps.a: Insert each domain into a trie keyed by the reversed label sequence (com → leetcode → discuss). Store the accumulated count at each node. A query for "com" traverses to the com node and returns the count stored there, which already includes all descendants. Query TC is O(L); build TC stays O(N × L).
